two-top/e7466bd:
A `Settings` resource — stick deadzone, haptics on/off, SFX + music volumes —
loaded from and saved to JSON in the platform config dir (dirs crate;
best-effort, in-memory if the dir can't resolve, e.g. some Android setups).

Wiring:
- Audio: every SFX cue reads `settings.sfx_volume` live; the ambient bed
  starts at `settings.music_volume` and a `sync_ambient_volume` system tracks
  changes live (the bed plays from boot, so a Title-screen change must reach
  the running sink).
- Haptics: each buzz is gated on `settings.haptics`.
- Deadzone: pushed into input_touch's new `StickDeadzone` resource, so it
  shapes the virtual stick *before* wire-quantization — a legal pre-wire input
  change, never post-wire (CONVENTIONS § input). The keyboard path is digital
  (deadzone-irrelevant); gamepads carry their own hardware deadzone.
- UI: a settings readout + adjustment keys on the title screen (H toggles
  haptics, -/= sfx, [ ] music, , . deadzone). Keys chosen to avoid the arena
  picker (1/2/3) and start (Space/Enter). Any change re-clamps + saves.

Settings::clamped() pins every field into range and replaces non-finite values
with defaults, so a hand-edited/corrupt file can't feed NaN into audio or
input. `#[serde(default)]` lets an older file missing a field still load.

Completes Task 5.5. Gate: 367 tests (incl. 3 settings round-trip/clamp/
partial-json), clippy --all-targets clean. App/input-side only — sim untouched,
determinism intact. Settings-screen runtime feel is operator-batched.

perennials/e7c2175:
The only place a decision survived was the address bar — fine for
sending a search, useless for standing in the yard in April wondering
what was picked in January. Keep is now a button on every plant page,
kept ids live in localStorage beside the spots, and the Kept tab lands
in the nav slot that has sat empty at repeat(3, 1fr) since the garden
view was cut.

The bloom calendar draws only over the kept list. USDA records a bloom
period for 1,071 of 8,800 plants, so across the catalogue the chart is
mostly holes; across twenty chosen plants it is an answer. The axis is
USDA's nine season words rather than months, because Late Spring is not
May in every zone, and the unqualified values (Spring, Summer,
Indeterminate) span their whole stretch instead of having a slot picked
for them. A plant with no recorded period is named beneath the grid,
never drawn as an empty row, which would read as does-not-flower — a
claim the data never made.
perennials/e73a80b:
The header read "Perr·enials". The rename sweep missed it because the word is
split across JSX elements, so "Perr" and "enials" are separate string literals
and a grep for "perren" finds nothing. It was the one piece of the misspelling
still on screen, on every screen. Per + · + ennials now spells it correctly with

Add a staleness notice. The dataset re-pulls itself weekly and the app keeps
serving the last good data if that fails, which is the right failure mode but a
silent one: a broken key or a changed upstream would quietly serve month-old
plants forever and nobody would know. Show nothing while it is healthy, and say
so plainly once the data passes two weeks old.
stoop/e71ac9f:
check.sh proves things about the files and cannot prove the app works.
Everything establishing that photos dither to two levels, that the sheet
keeps what was typed, that a merge keeps both people's notes, lived in a
scratch directory and would have died with the session that wrote it.

So the suites move into the repo. test/01-features.js covers renaming,
the joint-author filter, photo intake and its 1-bit output, panel and
photo persistence across a reload, the rendered sheet imposing as preset
A, and a full two-device export-and-merge. test/02-robustness.js covers
the states a notebook reaches after a year: corrupt storage, a backup
missing whole collections, a v2 notebook upgrading, photo references
whose blobs did not travel, an emptied log, sheet merge ordering, that
the bundle leaks no globals, and that a phone gets no sideways scroll.
Twenty-nine assertions, all passing.

The fixture is generated rather than committed: test/fixture.js writes a
PNG with node's own zlib, so the suite carries no binary and no image
library, and the intake pipeline is handed a real photograph-shaped
gradient with hard edges in it.

They stay optional on purpose. check.sh remains instant and free of
dependencies so the pre-commit hook can run on every commit; the suites
need a browser, so CONTRIBUTING asks for them on any commit touching
src/js or the press. PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM points at an existing binary
where the installed Playwright and the available browser disagree.
